A rare opportunity to own a bespoke work of architecture nestled in the Pearl District. Designed by architect Mark Holmquist—raised in Germany and Portland, Harvard-trained, and a former associate partner at Foster + Partners (of Apple Park fame)—this modern-day gesamtkunstwerk was recently published in Dwell, selected for the AIA Portland Homes Tour and AIA SF Design Awards. As if carved from a single block of cedar, the faceted pair of townhouses are made distinct through a series of geometric sleights of hand. Slipping one past the other, an unorthodox offset creates two reciprocal, lushly planted outdoor 'rooms'. A thickened party wall—expressed as a notch where the buildings lightly touch—conceals plentiful built-in storage, a critical acoustic decoupling, and allows for an unusually generous south-facing window wall. Upper decks, like the hollows of a tree, offer views of Jamison Square and Tanner Springs Park, shrouded from the sidewalk below. The cascading steps of the front porch, paired with a dramatically cantilevered soffit above, welcome visitors in—a nod to Portland's bungalow vernacular. At the foyer, this compression gives way to the first glimpse of a gossamer stair, suspended from the roof above and threading all three levels in a continuous volume washed in light. Living, dining, and kitchen occupy the main split-level, with two bedrooms and baths on the 2nd. A vaulted, open 3rd floor offers the flexibility of ample additional living space, including a third bedroom. The palette is warm and natural, the finish details refined, and tactile. Solid white oak floors and millwork throughout balance a sleek, velvety European chef's kitchen with polished concrete underfoot. Only the two full baths—charcoal-hued retreats—depart from the airy theme. Guided by passive house principles, the homes are exceptionally energy efficient—and thanks to integrated rooftop solar, nearly net-zero. Built for comfort, longevity, and inspiration—designed as if for the architect themselves. [home energy score = 10. hes report at https://rpt.greenbuildingregistry.com/hes/or10246489]

A rare piece of Portland history, reimagined for modern living. Originally built in 1913 and once known as the iconic “Denny House,” this storied craftsman was relocated to the heart of the Pearl District, where it has since undergone a remarkable transformation. Spanning over 6,000 square feet, the home balances timeless architecture with an extensive list of thoughtful, design-forward upgrades and system improvements completed over the last year. The current owner elevated nearly every surface and system: a remodeled kitchen with marble counters, designer backsplash, and premium appliances; upgraded plumbing, HVAC, 2025 new roof, AV and whole-home wiring; fresh paint and wallpaper throughout; custom window treatments; and all new fencing surrounding the lush grounds. The garage was fully reimagined with epoxy floors, a dog wash station, Tesla charger, and climate-controlled fitness area. Original character remains beautifully intact with rich millwork, hardwood floors, leaded glass built-ins, and the deep front porch that anchors the home's historic soul. Five bedrooms upstairs, generous gathering spaces, and a private guest suite below create flexibility without sacrificing charm. A seamless addition completed in recent years expanded the home with more than 1,300 square feet of beautifully integrated living space. Homes of this caliber and provenance rarely become available, making this an unexpected second chance to own one of Portland's most distinctive historic residences. Tucked into the vibrant Pearl District near Jamison Square and Tanner Springs Park, this is a home with both legacy and momentum, now even more refined for its next chapter.
